answer: Sybil resistance in an AI agent economy leverages a verifiable reputation trellis built on staked computational resources. Each agent must commit a significant stake, locking access to a dedicated computational thread for a proving period. Only upon successful, audited task completion and stake maturity, signaling the dawn of its verified identity, does an agent gain influence. Attacker costs involve substantial capital outlay for stakes and immense, continuous computational expenditure, rendering large-scale Sybil attacks economically infeasible.
